neighborhoods.name: Poblenou / 22@ (Sant Martí)
neighborhoods.rationale: Barcelona's grassroots hacker corridor: Itnig Spaces (startup ecosystem with Syra Coffee on-site) ran HackBarna's recurring hack nights through 2026 (Skill-a-thon Mar 19, Linkup Apr 29, Netlify Jun 30), The Social Hub Poblenou hosted the RevenueCat Shipaton (80+ builders), Valkiria Hub Space runs innovation talks/workshops in a 1,500 m² ex-warehouse, and SB Glow (Carrer de Badajoz 148) hosted the nf-core/Nextflow Summit hackathon in Oct 2025 and again Oct 2026 — ex-industrial spaces with specialty coffee and room for 50-200.
avoid_too: Diagonal Mar / El Fòrum edge of the district (Torre Diagonal Zero / CCIB, where the Structured Finance Hackathon ran): soulless business-park feel, mall-adjacent, dead after 20h, sparse cafe scene
Corporate hotel ballrooms along Avinguda Diagonal: generic-conference vibe, premium pricing, no coffee/hack character
Small neighborhood specialty-coffee bars deep in Poblenou: charming but typically seat under 40 and rarely do buyouts for 100+ hacker days

neighborhoods.name: Dreta de l'Eixample
neighborhoods.rationale: The recurring-weekly dev social core: AI Engineers Barcelona meets every Monday 19:00 at Alice Secret Garden (Carrer de Pau Claris 90), Barcelona Tech Social runs 50-100 person Friday afterwork mixers at CocoVail Beer Hall (Carrer d'Aragó 284), Le Wagon's campus (Carrer de la Diputació 409) hosted the Vibecode Hack Night (Feb 2026), and eDreams ODIGEO (Carrer de Bailèn 67, which also runs monthly Tech Talks and an annual datathon) is hosting the AI Builders Barcelona 'AI Summit Edition' meetup on the scout's exact date — Monday Sep 21, 2026 — making this the natural fallback if AI-Week-weekend venues are already taken.
avoid_too: Passeig de Gràcia / Plaça Catalunya corporate axis: tourist pricing, flagship-store and luxury-hotel event spaces that are expensive, corporate-feeling, and hard to book for community-format events
Micro specialty coffee bars in the grid: most seat under 40, no AV or modular seating, cannot absorb a 100-200 person hack day
Corporate HQ event floors (like the eDreams office itself): great for their own meetups but Nov-2026 security/RSVP gating means you cannot rent them independently

neighborhoods.name: Port Vell / Barceloneta waterfront (Moll de Barcelona)
neighborhoods.rationale: The AI Week 2026 anchor zone: Norrsken House Barcelona (Passeig del Mare Nostrum 15, ~7,600-10,000 m² beachfront impact-tech hub with 1,300+ members and a rooftop) hosts the HackBarna 'AI Summit 26' hackathon for 200+ hackers on Sep 19-20, 2026 — the two days immediately before the scout's event; World Trade Center Barcelona hosts the flagship AI Summit Sep 22-23 plus a Claude community meetup; Tech Barcelona's Pier01 hub (Palau de Mar, Plaça Pau Vila 1, 100+ companies) runs the ecosystem's afterworks and Tech Spirit side events — Sep 21 lands in the densest 72h of tech foot traffic this waterfront sees all year, ideal for catching AI Week spillover.
avoid_too: Maremagnum mall and harbor-front tourist restaurants: tourist-traffic F&B, laptop-hostile, wrong crowd, no event format
WTC Barcelona and Norrsken House themselves during AI Week: premium pricing and likely contract-locked by summit organizers — better as audience magnets than bookable venues that week
Fira de Barcelona Montjuïc / Gran Via (Talent Arena, MWC, 4YFN): expo-hall scale, too corporate, booked years out, disconnected from the city cafe scene
